about: The third video, a full demo of Study Stash: the contract it is built to. Each scene starts at `start` (seconds), its narration line at `vo`; every effect is at `at` (seconds, in this plan's own times). `listed` effects are the ones on Joey's ElevenLabs list; the rest are clicks the pointer makes on the way (the same soft click). `npm run demo-audio` reads this, fits the narration (a scene whose line runs long is stretched on the beat and everything after it moves, effects included), and writes the final times to src/demo/timeline.json, which the video plays.

scenes.line: This is Study Stash. Your lectures, written up and filed by class.
scenes.shows: The black intro: the icon drawn in light, “Study Stash” rising, “Your lectures, written up and filed by class.”, glimpses of what’s to come
scenes.direction: warm and confident; a small beat after "Study Stash"

scenes.line: Setting up is quick. Pick your AI, and it walks you through the rest.
scenes.shows: Guided setup: Welcome to Study Stash, Claude picked; Claude’s chat: Just this Mac, Set up; the microphone check; You’re set up, Open Study Stash; the notification pointing at the S. in the menu bar

scenes.line: Press record when class starts. The words show up as they're said, and the recording never leaves your computer.
scenes.shows: The menu bar’s S. opens its dropdown; Record · BIO 110; the recorder’s pill (red dot, time, level meter); the recorder opens and the live words come in; “50 minutes later”; Stop; “Recording saved”
scenes.direction: clear; a little lift on "as they're said", sincere on the last part

scenes.line: Stop, and your notes are written for you, filed in the right class. The diagrams follow a minute later.
scenes.shows: The library, BIO 110: “Writing the notes…” as the clock moves on; filed (the list, the count, the notification); the notes open with “Adding diagrams…”; “A minute later”; the diagram drops in; “Diagrams added”

scenes.line: Every diagram is alive. Point at a box to see what it connects to, pin it, ask about it, step through it, or hide the words and test yourself.
scenes.shows: The cardiac cycle diagram: a box lit with its neighbours, pinned (Explain this, Quiz me, Where was this said?, Zoom in); Step through, Next; Test yourself, a hidden box checked, Knew it
scenes.direction: curious; the list with momentum, a little playful on "test yourself"

scenes.line: Formulas become graphs you can drag, so you can see what every number does.
scenes.shows: CS 340’s notes: the sigmoid’s steepness slider dragged; gradient descent’s learning rate dragged down, then up

scenes.line: When a lecture describes something, like a drone or a hand, your notes can draw it, labelled.
scenes.shows: ENGR 120’s drone: the battery passed, the flight controller lit and pinned (its card); then NURS 210’s hand, a tendon lit
scenes.direction: a spark of delight on "draw it"

scenes.line: Ask anything about your lectures, and get answers from what was actually said in class.
scenes.shows: CS 101’s notes with the Ask bar: “What’s on the midterm?” typed and sent; the answer written in from what was said

scenes.line: Connect Canvas to see what's due next, with every assignment's details in one place.
scenes.shows: Due: soonest first, the late one marked Missing; Lab 3 opened: due date, points, instructions, rubric

scenes.line: Your library comes with you on your phone: your notes, what's due, and Ask.
scenes.shows: The phone app: Library; a tap into The cardiac cycle’s notes; the Due tab; the Ask tab
scenes.direction: light; a small pause at the colon

scenes.line: Make it yours. Turn rich notes on or off, use Claude Code's fast mode, or write lectures down after class, so your laptop stays quiet.
scenes.shows: Settings → AI engines: Rich notes switched off; Claude Code speed → Fast mode; Recording: When it’s written down → After class
scenes.direction: relaxed; a list, settling down on "stays quiet"

scenes.line: Connect Claude, Codex or Gemini to your library in one click.
scenes.shows: Settings → AI tool access: Connect, for Claude Desktop; “Added. Quit and reopen…”; then “Connected · started 13:41”

scenes.line: Your recordings never leave your computers. Free and open source, for Mac and Windows.
scenes.shows: The drawn laptop that locks; “Your recordings stay on your computer.”; “Free and open source, for Mac and Windows.”
scenes.direction: sincere, a touch slower; a beat between the sentences

scenes.shows: The end card: the icon, Study Stash, Free for Mac and Windows, study-stash-app.web.app; held to the last frame
scenes.direction: warm and confident, a beat after "Study Stash"

sounds.prompt: Very soft, gentle airy whoosh for a slide transition, low and smooth, soft air moving, no hiss, no reverb tail
Very soft trackpad click, a single muted tap, close-miked, dry, no reverb, no high-pitched tick
Soft rounded start-recording sound, a low muted thup with a gentle rise, like a small button pressed into felt, dry, no beep, no bell, no chime
Soft rounded interface pop, like a small card settling into place, a gentle low wooden tok, dry, no bell, no chime, no reverb
Soft airy shimmer, a breath of light rising, like a gentle brush sweep over fine sand, warm and quiet, no bells, no chimes, no ringing tones
Soft friction of a small knob slid smoothly along a track, quiet and steady, close-miked, no clicks, no ticks
Quiet laptop typing, about two seconds of soft key presses, low muted thocks, a short sentence typed at an easy pace, dry, no clatter
One soft tap of a fingertip on a phone's glass screen, muted and rounded, very short, dry, no click, no tick
Warm soft swell of a felt piano and string pad chord in D major, rising gently over a second then fading over three seconds, calm and hopeful, no bells, no chimes, no percussion

music.prompt: Warm, light instrumental bed for a calm product demo: a soft pad in D major, a gentle plucked arpeggio, soft drums coming in around 0:15, a quieter breakdown for the last fifteen seconds and a warm final chord, 120 BPM, no vocals, no bells, no chimes
music.note: Under everything, from the first frame to the last, dipping under each line; at 120 BPM every scene starts on a beat.
